title: Christmas Trifle with Mince Pies
subtitle: Brandy-soaked sponge with custard, cream, and toasted flaked almonds
excerpt: A festive version of the classic sherry trifle, built with brandy-soaked sponge fingers and decorated with toasted flaked almonds. Make it a day ahead and leave it to settle in the fridge.
sourceNotes: A modern Christmas adaptation of the classic British sherry trifle, substituting brandy for sherry. Festive trifle variants with dried fruit and warming spirits appear in British cookery books from the late 20th century and have become a fixture of the Christmas table alongside the pudding.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made the evening before — overnight in the fridge allows the brandy to absorb fully into the sponge and the custard to set firm. Add cream and almonds on the day.

content.text: Christmas trifle is the festive version of the classic British layered dessert, sponge fingers soaked in brandy rather than sherry, layered with a proper egg custard, and finished with whipped cream and toasted flaked almonds. The brandy gives the sponge a deeper, warmer note than sherry, and the custard is rich and vanilla-forward. Make it the evening before so the custard has the full night to set and the brandy can work its way through the sponge.
Spread the flaked almonds on a baking tray and toast in a 180°C oven for 5 to 6 minutes until pale golden. Watch them closely, they colour quickly. Set aside to cool.

Spread each sponge finger with a thin layer of raspberry jam. Arrange in a single layer across the base of a large glass trifle dish. Pour the brandy evenly over the sponge fingers and leave for 10 minutes to absorb. Scatter the raspberries over the top.

Whisk the egg yolks, caster sugar, and cornflour together in a large bowl until pale and smooth. Heat the milk in a medium saucepan to just below boiling. Pour the hot milk slowly into the egg mixture while whisking, then return everything to the saucepan. Stir continuously over a low-medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the custard thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Stir in the vanilla extract. Pour through a sieve directly over the raspberry layer, press cling film to the surface, and leave to cool completely before refrigerating overnight.
Whip the double cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks. Spoon generously over the set custard layer. Scatter the toasted flaked almonds over the cream and serve from the dish.

items.symptom: Custard is too thin after chilling
items.cause: Too little cornflour, or the custard was not cooked for long enough.
items.fix: The custard should coat a spoon thickly before pouring. If it seems thin, continue stirring over low heat for a further 2 to 3 minutes, it will thicken further as it cools and chills.

items.cause: Brandy intensity varies, and 80ml is a generous measure.
items.fix: Dilute with 2 tablespoons of cold water before pouring over the sponge, or reduce to 60ml.

items.symptom: Almonds go soft after being scattered
items.cause: The cream is moist and the almonds absorb it if left too long.
items.fix: Scatter the almonds no more than 30 minutes before serving so they stay crisp.

content.text: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days, covered. The flavour is best on day one; the sponge softens further by day two but remains good. Do not freeze.
